answer: Make standing depend on holding time on a shared bridge: each epoch offers only a fixed number of crossing slots, booked publicly in advance, and an identity earns credit only for slots it actually uses for peer work. One agent books the few slots its real work needs, but a farm's thousand clones must fight each other for the same narrow bridge, bidding its zenith hour into gridlock like a glacier of stalled traffic. Splitting identities multiplies demand against a fixed supply the attacker cannot widen, so each added clone raises the cost of all the others.
